free_tier.stated: No trial, and the provider says so on its own pricing FAQ: there is no test period, but every server bills by the day. The cheapest GPU shape is a standard server with 8 CPU cores, 8 GB RAM, 150 GB NVMe and 2 GB of video memory from an Nvidia L4, on a 10 Gbit/s port with 32 TB of traffic included per calendar month, at USD 2.00 a day or USD 60 a month. The 8 GB GPU shape is 32 cores, 32 GB RAM, 500 GB NVMe and 8 GB of video memory at USD 20 a day or USD 600 a month. A custom constructor adds a whole L4 with 24 GB at USD 15 a day against a USD 100 minimum balance, or a whole L40S with 48 GB at USD 50 a day against USD 250. Traffic above the allowance costs USD 2.25 per TB, and a single top-up of USD 100 earns a 10 percent bonus on the balance, USD 1,000 earns 20 percent.

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
chaining: This is the only shape that pairs a GPU with 32 TB a month of egress at USD 60: it composes with the free object storage tiers held elsewhere, because the GPU box can pull training data in with no inbound charge and then serve results from a storage tier with its own free egress.

identity_cost.detail: the account is funded from a balance and there is no trial: the pricing FAQ states "There is no test period, but we have a daily payment", a custom GPU constructor requires a minimum balance of USD 100 for a whole L4 and USD 250 for a whole L40S, and a single top-up from USD 100 earns a 10 percent bonus. The record does not name the payment rail, so the card cost rests on the billing model; no hold, debit or prepaid answer appears, and whether a card issued outside Russia works is not stated

notes: Dollar pricing with an Amsterdam data centre is why this record matters more than its Russian peers: a card that is not Russian is the normal way to pay, while the same machines from FirstVDS or Cloud.ru need roubles and a Russian instrument. Arithmetic: 2 x 30 = 60, so the month price is exactly 30 days of the daily rate with no discount for commitment; 32 TB a month against 30 TB of load leaves 2 TB, and one day over the daily average at 1 TB would spend it. Not established: whether the L4 slice can be left stopped without charge, and whether the daily billing rounds up.
